## Profiles

A [profile](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/configure/profiles) is a complete VS Code set-up: settings, keybindings, snippets, tasks, extensions and UI state. Each folder remembers which profile it was last opened with.

| Profile | Used for |
|---|---|
| `R` | All daily R work, on every machine. The one documented on [Settings](settings.qmd), [Keybindings](keybindings.qmd) and [Extensions](extensions.qmd). |
| `R-Lecturer` | Teaching: VS Code's defaults plus what is needed to run R. See [below](#the-r-lecturer-profile). |
| Default | Folders that are not R projects, and the place for application-wide settings (see below). |

My other profiles are unrelated to R and not covered here.

### Profiles do not inherit

A non-default profile's `settings.json` replaces the Default one; it is not layered on top. Precedence is:

1. VS Code's built-in defaults,
2. the active profile's settings (Default *or* `R` *or* `R-Lecturer`, never a mix),
3. the workspace settings (`.vscode/settings.json` in the project).

So every profile must contain everything it needs. That is why the `R` profile repeats most of the Default settings.

The one exception is application-scoped settings, such as `update.mode` and `settingsSync.ignoredSettings`. They apply to the whole VS Code installation and are read only from the Default profile; other profiles show them greyed out.

### Where the files are

| What | Path |
|---|---|
| Default profile settings | `%APPDATA%\Code\User\settings.json` |
| Other profiles | `%APPDATA%\Code\User\profiles\<profile id>\settings.json` (also `keybindings.json`, `tasks.json`, `snippets\`) |
| Profile names, and which folder uses which profile | `%APPDATA%\Code\User\globalStorage\storage.json` |

To move a folder to another profile, open it and pick the profile in the gear menu (bottom left).

## Settings Sync

[Settings Sync](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/configure/settings-sync) keeps profiles, settings, keybindings, snippets, tasks, extensions and UI state the same on every machine where you sign in. Change a setting once, on any machine, and it travels. That only works if the synced files contain no machine-specific paths ([How the pieces fit](index.qmd#how-the-pieces-fit)).

### The gotcha: some settings never sync {#the-gotcha}

Sync silently skips three kinds of settings:

- those marked *machine* (they only make sense on one computer),
- those marked *machine-overridable*,
- those flagged *never to sync* by their extension.

vscode-R marks several of its settings like that: `r.consolePath`, `r.executablePath`, `r.consoleArgs`, `r.consoleSendDelay` and `r.plot.backend`.

The fix is the `settingsSync.ignoredSettings` list. A leading `-` means "include this after all":

```json
"settingsSync.ignoredSettings": ["-r.consolePath", "-r.plot.backend"]
```

- It must be in the Default profile, where VS Code reads application-scoped settings. I keep the same line in each synced profile as well.
- To see what was uploaded: *Settings Sync: Show Synced Data*.

The two settings it opts back in are safe to sync because they hold no paths: `r.consolePath` is just `"radian"` (found on `PATH`), and `r.plot.backend` is `"httpgd"`.

### What Settings Sync does not carry {#what-settings-sync-does-not-carry}

| Not synced | Where it lives | How I keep it in step |
|---|---|---|
| R, Rtools, Python, radian, Quarto, R packages | installed per machine | [Install, in order](install.qmd), the same versions everywhere |
| `PATH` and environment variables | Windows | the [PATH rules](outside_vscode.qmd#path-rules) |
| Task scripts | `%USERPROFILE%\.vscode-scripts\` | copied by hand ([Snippets and tasks](snippets_tasks.qmd)) |
| `.Rprofile` | `Documents\.Rprofile` | OneDrive shares the Documents folder ([Outside VS Code](outside_vscode.qmd#rprofile)) |
| PowerShell profiles | `Documents\PowerShell\` | OneDrive, as above |
| Which folder uses which profile | `storage.json` | set per machine (gear menu) |

### Different from the R profile, or only here

| Setting | Value | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `workbench.colorTheme` | `"Visual Studio 2019 Dark"` | Colour theme. |
| `editor.unicodeHighlight.nonBasicASCII` | `true` | Highlights non-ASCII characters. |
| `[markdown]` | markdownlint as formatter | Formats Markdown with markdownlint. |
| `editor.formatOnPaste` | `true` | Formats pasted code. |
| `remote.SSH.remotePlatform` | `"linux"` for each of my servers | Tells Remote - SSH the OS of each server, so it does not ask. |
| `update.mode` | `"start"` | Checks for VS Code updates only at start-up. |
| `update.enableWindowsBackgroundUpdates` | `false` | Does not download and install updates in the background. |
| `window.menuBarVisibility` | `"classic"` | Always shows the menu bar. |
| `grammarly.files.include` | Markdown, text, R, Quarto, R Markdown | Files Grammarly checks. |
| `grammarly.config.documentDialect` | `"british"` | British English. |
| `grammarly.config.documentDomain` | `"academic"` | Academic writing style. |
| `grammarly.config.suggestions.OxfordComma` | `true` | Suggests the Oxford comma. |
| `grammarly.startTextCheckInPausedState` | `true` | Grammarly starts paused; turn it on when writing. |
| `chatgpt.localeOverride` | `"en-US"` | Codex extension (`openai.chatgpt`): the language of its interface. |
| `mssql.enableRichExperiences` | `true` | Newer UI of the SQL Server extension. |

```{r}
#| echo: false

show_file(
  "Default/settings.json", "json",
  label = "Default profile settings.json"
)
```

## The R-Lecturer profile {#the-r-lecturer-profile}

My teaching profile keeps VS Code's defaults and adds only what is needed to run R:

- radian as the R console and httpgd for plots (`r.consolePath`, `r.bracketedPaste`, `r.plot.backend`; needs the `httpgd` R package), with the same `settingsSync.ignoredSettings` line as `R`;
- the Light Modern theme, for the projector;
- no Copilot completions;
- Quarto previews in the browser, and the visual editor wraps at 80 columns and spell-checks in British English.

Its only extensions are vscode-R (`reditorsupport.r`, `reditorsupport.r-syntax`) and Quarto (`quarto.quarto`); Copilot Chat ships with VS Code. It has no keybindings, tasks or snippets of its own.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
show_file(
  "R-Lecturer/settings.json", "json",
  label = "R-Lecturer settings.json"
)
```
